title: performance canary: enhanced auto-detection and rollout guards
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds improved canary detection using bootstrap-based latency and throughput regression tests and automatic rollout guards that pause or rollback canaries on significant regressions. Includes observability dashboard updates and an opt-in config to tune sensitivity.
description: Motivation: We need more reliable automatic detection of performance regressions in canaries and stronger rollout guards to prevent large customer-facing regressions. This PR implements a bootstrap-based statistical detector for latency and throughput regressions, integrates it into the perf-canary pipeline, and adds runtime rollout guards that automatically pause traffic or fall back to a safe model variant when a regression is detected. Summary of changes: 1) detector module with bootstrap confidence intervals and FDR-adjusted thresholds; 2) integration with canary scheduler to evaluate windows and emit decisions; 3) rollout guard controller that can pause traffic, set traffic to 0, and trigger configured alerting hooks (PagerDuty/Slack); 4) perf job updates and new unit + integration tests; 5) observability/dashboard + runbook updates. See linked linear tasks for background. This description is intentionally continuous and includes checklist below. Checklist: - [x] detector algorithm implemented and unit-tested - [x] end-to-end perf tests added - [x] rollout guard controller implemented - [x] docs and dashboard updated - [x] feature gated behind runtime canary flag Implementation notes: The detector uses bootstrapped sampling of per-request latency and throughput distributions over sliding windows, computes median and tail quantiles, and compares against control using a two-sided test with FDR correction. When the detector reports a significant regression above configured sensitivity, the rollout guard controller first reduces canary traffic to 0 and then marks the deployment as paused. Alerts include context (metric deltas, sample sizes, CI for the delta) to help triage. Backwards compatibility: The feature is behind a runtime flag and default sensitivity matches existing heuristic behavior. Rollout plan: gated rollout to Dedicated clusters for one week, observe alerts and false positive rate, then ramp wider.

notes: This change reduces alert noise by applying FDR correction but increases CPU cost on the scheduler due to bootstrap sampling. We added a sampling cap and async evaluation to keep latency impact minimal. Monitoring to watch: scheduler CPU, false_positive_rate, canary_pauses.
